The overnight story is oil. WTI is down 4.50% to 86.74 and Brent is down 4.74% to 93.66. The drop follows Trump's comment that new attacks on Iran are 'highly unlikely' if Tehran agrees a nuclear deal and reopens Hormuz, and it has set off a futures-led relief bid. ES is +0.93% at 7470.5, NQ +0.96% and Dow futures +1.30%. Europe is trading live and higher: Euro Stoxx 50 +1.50%, STOXX 600 +1.07%, FTSE +0.78%. The Nikkei closed +2.33%. Prior session: the S&P 500 finished +0.31% at 7376.86 and the Nasdaq +1.09% at 24579.42, while the Dow lost 0.46%. The VIX closed at 23.18, down 9.59%. Sentiment is tentatively better, but the credit tape argues for caution. - **Junk-bond (HY) contagion:** The gap between Caa (CCC) and single-B spreads is 766bp, against a 5-year average of 418bp. That is the 99th percentile of the past five years and the widest since April 2020. It is +199bp over three months, even though it narrowed 15bp last week. The stress is starting to move up the quality ladder. Single-B is +29bp over one month and +63bp over three, and Ba is +16bp over one month. The B–Ba gap (119bp, 50th percentile of 5 years) and IG (+10bp in a month at 91bp) have barely moved. The 63-day Caa/B correlation has risen from 0.35 three months ago to 0.66 now, close to its 0.69 five-year median. This is descriptive, not a validated signal. Read it as: CCC rot is leaking into single-B but has not reached BB or IG. - **AI backstop:** CoreWeave 5Y CDS is 1270bp. That is 75.5bp above the 1,194.5bp Oct 15 record, 818bp above the June low, and +160bp on the week, even after tightening 43bp versus Friday. Nvidia CDS is unmoved at 143.56bp (-2.5bp on the day, -3.9bp on the week). Meta and Microsoft tightened on the week, and only Oracle widened (+12.95bp). The market is clearly not buying a full Nvidia backstop of the neoclouds. It is pricing CoreWeave as a stand-alone credit, with its notes near 77–82 and yields of about 16%, while treating Nvidia's own balance sheet as safe. In short, it does not expect the guarantor to be dragged in. This too is descriptive, not a signal. - **Tech-analog phase model:** The model keeps the tech basket in Phase 1 (initial drop, credit calm). The basket is down 21.24% versus 14.93% for the 2000 basket on the same day. Three signposts are triggered: CoreWeave CDS above its record, 78.6% of basket names more than 20% off their highs, and SOX 35.84% off its 52-week high. HY OAS is still 112bp short of its Phase-2 trigger. The model puts Phase 2 at 27.0% over 6 months, and the chance of reaching Phase 2 or worse within 12 months at 58.7%, down 15.5pp from the prior run. With markets pricing a likely Warsh hike on Dec 8–9 (CME FedWatch about 77–85%), this looks like a relief rally to rent, not a regime change.

NY Harbor ULSD (US Diesel) — current: 424.66 cents/gal vs WTI

NY Harbor ULSD is trading at 424.66 cents/gal, and all five gauges sit in the high zone at historical extremes. Two-sided analog episodes per signal: days where the signal's percentile-rank (vs its own full history) was <=5th or >=95th, or |z-score|>=1.3, clustered into one episode per zone per >=6-month gap between episode starts. For each zone, the realized forward 6-month % change in the BENCHMARK'S OUTRIGHT PRICE from each episode start is measured; a card's direction (BUY/SELL) is whichever sign that median historical move carries. Entry/target/stretch/stop are computed directly from this table -- the narrative prose (thesis/rationale) is the only part supplied by an LLM, and it is not permitted to alter a number. Crack spreads and curve shapes are, financially, relative-value signals rather than clean predictors of outright price; expressing every card in outright price terms is a deliberate simplification. HO36 Comdty (ULSD's 36-month point) is thin/less liquid on this seat -- treat its curve-shape reading with lower confidence than the others. Not investment advice.

Churn = the longest window of 20-120 sessions whose close range is <= 8x its median ATR(14), with median ADX(14) < 20, an insignificant close-price slope (p > 0.05), and >= 2 entries into each edge zone (top/bottom 20% of the band). Support/resistance = median swing low/high (+/-5 sessions); outer edges = the window's extreme closes. Breakout = a close beyond the outer edge by > 0.5 ATR, confirmed by a second close or one close beyond 1 ATR. A break back inside within 5 sessions is a failed break. An episode's outer edges can widen at most 0.5 ATR past their first detection, so a slow grind can't drag the range along with it. Base rates come from replaying the same rules over the full history, day by day, with no lookahead. This is pattern analysis of historical prices, not investment advice.

💧Treasury liquidity & rates volcomputed

US Govt Securities Liquidity Index (GVLQUSD), MOVE, Fed DKW term premium and TLT option skew, live from Bloomberg + federalreserve.gov.

Five charts tracking the mechanism Simon White laid out for why Treasury liquidity is deteriorating: rising inflation volatility feeds into a higher term premium, which steepens the curve, which raises bond vol, which shows up as worse UST market liquidity. Right now UST liquidity is at the 50th percentile of its own history (higher = worse) and the Fed's own DKW real term premium is +79bp.

Latest reading is +0.67 vol points (45th percentile of the 64 runs recorded so far). Positive means the 5%-OTM put is pricier than the at-the-money option -- the market paying up for downside-price / higher-yield insurance on long-end Treasuries.

UST liquidity index is 1.53 (50th percentile of its own 2007-present history -- 100th = worst liquidity on record), improving over the past 3 months (-0.08 pts). CPI YoY volatility (2yr) is 0.50pp; the article's thesis is that rising inflation vol drags liquidity worse, which this chart is built to let you check month to month.

Real term premium is +79bp (90th percentile of its own 2007-present history), up 1bp over the trailing ~2 months. Inflation risk premium is +11bp. Fed staff's own DKW decomposition (D'Amico-Kim-Wei, updated Kim-Walsh-Wei) splits the rise in long yields into a policy-uncertainty component (real term premium) and an inflation-uncertainty component -- both rising is the article's read that this move isn't just a rate-expectations story.

MOVE is 92.8 (66th percentile of its own post-2007 history). The 3m10s curve is 75bp (flatter by 10bp over 3 months). The article's claim is mechanical, not just correlated -- a steeper curve gives forward rates more room to move before converging to spot, which is itself higher realized/implied vol.

MOVE and the UST liquidity index have moved together with a full-history correlation of +0.72 (both series read as 'worse' when they rise). That's the closing link in the article's chain: inflation vol -> term premium -> curve steepness -> bond vol -> liquidity.

TLT skew accumulates one point per report run -- Bloomberg's option-surface field is snapshot-only, not retrievable historically via the API. Term premium is the Fed's own DKW model series (D'Amico-Kim-Wei, updated Kim-Walsh-Wei), pulled directly from federalreserve.gov, not Bloomberg. Not a trading signal -- a liquidity/vol monitor only.

Same test on each trailing window: cup base = lowest close in the window, left rim = highest close before it, right rim = highest close after it. Cup complete at ≥90% retracement; above 110% the yield has run past the old high (a breakout, not a cup). No cup inside the window when its left rim is not the highest close of the 91 days before it, i.e. yields were already falling into the window. Pass level = cup base + 0.90 × (left rim − cup base).

🗞️Street View — Where the Cycle Is HeadingCURATED · AS OF 2026-10-01

⚠ Commentary is 39 days old (as of 2026-10-01); it may not reflect the latest Fed news.

Consensus is a short, shallow campaign: one or two more 25bp hikes, December more likely than October. The debate is whether hiking into an energy shock ends in recession, and the bond market is already doing some of the tightening.

The Fed

  • Sept 16: unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%, the first since 2023. Dots: median one more hike in 2026; 16 of 18 see at least one, 4 see two. Inflation not back at 2% until 2029. (CNBC, FedAndMarkets)
  • Warsh's message was distinctly hawkish (inflation 'too high and broad-based'); the Conference Board calls it 'not a one and done'. (Conference Board)
  • Sept 29, Williams (NY Fed): 'no need for urgency'; one more hike 'late this year' may be appropriate; the biggest inflation shocks have passed. (Bloomberg, NY Fed)
  • Sept 30, August PCE came in soft: headline 3.4% (vs 3.7% expected), core 3.0% (vs 3.3%). October odds fell; December still priced. Kashkari: inflation 'still too high'. (CNBC, CNBC (Kashkari))

Market pricing

  • October 28 hike odds vary widely by venue, roughly 35% to 69% (prediction markets highest, CME futures ~58%), mostly measured before the soft PCE print. (PredictionMarketsPicks)
  • About 83% odds of another hike by year-end; futures price ~93bp of tightening over the next 9 meetings, more than the dots. (Forbes)

Bonds and credit

  • 10-year Treasury above 5.25% (Sept 28), the highest since 2007; 30-year ~5.49%. Drivers cited: sticky energy inflation (Iran war), heavy issuance, AI capex demand. Term premium ~1.0–1.4%. (CNBC, CNBC (Warsh's yield problem))
  • AI-related issuers trade ~115bp vs ~78bp for IG overall; high-yield AI supply $40B year to date vs $12B in all of 2025. BNP and Goldman warn the issuance could pressure spreads. (Reuters, Bloomberg (BNP))

The bear case

  • Rosenberg: the Fed has never hiked into an energy shock without a recession, and AI won't save it this time. (TheStreet)
  • Goldman called the case for hiking 'weak' (demand not overheating, energy inflation should fade when the war ends). Oxford Economics: 'The Fed cannot control energy prices'; the risk is a weaker labor market. (CNN)

Read-through: For bonds, the bigger risk is the long end, not the Fed: term premium and supply keeping the 10-year above 5% matter more than one extra 25bp. The recession call is loud but isn't in any sell-side house view yet.

🔥Is Inflation Persistent?

Persistence score: 58/100 — Underlying inflation is moderately persistent but slowly cooling. The cyclical core is stuck in the mid-2s while the volatile edge runs hot. Median CPI (2.61%, falling) is the only core measure trending down; trimmed-mean, median PCE and core sticky CPI are flat at 2.26–2.78%. The breadth data says the problem is not over: in the Dallas distribution 16.6% of the PCE basket is rising faster than 10% and another 10.2% at 5–10%. Flexible CPI is 6.12% and rising. Today's oil collapse should help the flexible side, and the 1y breakeven at 1.94% shows markets expect it to. For a Fed that calls inflation 'too high', though, headline Core PCE at 3.12% keeps a December hike on the table. Verdict: sticky, not accelerating; the risk is breadth, not trend.

🫧Tech Bubble Peak Again?vs March 2000

9 of 22 indicators at peak-like levels · 6 beyond 2000 — 59/100
Today is far from March 2000 on equity froth but close to, or past, it on credit complacency, which is classic late-cycle. Equity Froth is the coolest dimension: - Nasdaq trailing P/E 38.27x versus 175x in 2000 (15% of the way to the peak). - Nasdaq 2.1% below its 200DMA (0% stretch). - SOX P/E 32.21x (31%). Late-cycle Catalysts run hot on credit: - IG spread tightness at 124% and Baa–10Y at 156% of 2000 conditions. - Financial conditions (NFCI -0.46) at 148%. - The 2s10s curve (31.94bp) at 68%. - PMIs are not rolling over (1% and 13%). Macro Regime shows commodities-vs-equities at 200% and the dollar at 39%. Bear-market signposts are mixed. VIX complacency reads 100%, but sentiment is washed out: AAII bull–bear spread at -14.3 (14%) and consumer confidence at 31%. The tech-analog phase model places the basket in Phase 1, an initial drop with calm credit. It is 23 days past the Oct 6 peak and down 21.24%, versus 14.93% for the 2000 basket at the same point. The model puts the 6-month odds at 48.6% Phase 1, 27.0% Phase 2, 10.5% Phase 3 and 13.9% Phase 4. It puts the chance of reaching Phase 2 or worse at 45.8% within 6 months and 58.7% within 12 months. These are model estimates, not certainties. Three signposts have already tripped: CoreWeave CDS, breadth and SOX. The market-wide credit trigger (HY at 448bp) has not.

Bubble-analog — today's Nasdaq vs the dot-com cycle (two anchors)

WHY TWO START DATES?
Each line is rebased to 100 at a low the tech bull launched from, so elapsed time lines up. Oct-2022 is today's anchor — it was the prior bear-market bottom. Oct-1990 is the dot-com cycle's equivalent (its literal prior bear bottom). But 1990 predates the internet mania by ~4 years, so the second chart re-anchors the dot-com line to the 1994 reset low, just before the surge ignited, for a tighter like-for-like. Today sits very early under the strict 1990 analog, further along under the 1994 surge analog.
━ Anchored at the prior bear-market bottom (Oct-1990)   ━ today's cycle
━ Anchored at the pre-internet reset low (1994)   ━ today's cycle

Valuation marker: today's Nasdaq P/E (38x) ≈ 22% of the ~175x 2000-peak P/E.

IF THIS RHYMES WITH 2000
Nasdaq fell -78.0% peak→trough (2000-03-10 → 2002-10-09, ~31 months); it took ~15 years to reclaim the high.

This is a bust starting in the tech basket while credit still believes the cycle is fine. The 2000 bubble was a valuation mania. Today's is a concentration-and-capex story. The top-10 weight is roughly 39% (analyst estimate, sourced to about 39–40% in 2026 coverage), against about 26–27% in 2000. CAPE is near 39x (analyst estimate; 2026 coverage cites 40–42 before the selloff). The pain is showing up first in the AI-infrastructure credit chain: CoreWeave CDS is above its record, its notes yield about 16%, and its equity is down 66% from its high. It is not showing up in mega-cap multiples. The HMM regime reading (99.6% 'Calm, Phase-1-like') and credit-calm probability of 97.3% say the broad market has not joined. The CCC–B gap at the 99th percentile of 5 years is the bridge to watch. The phase model's tilt, historically, has favoured gold, Treasury duration and IG credit over mega-cap growth, developed international and EM. IPO froth is moderate: Anthropic is marketing at a lowered valuation target, which is a sign of discipline, not mania. Long-term EPS-growth expectations remain elevated on AI hopes (analyst estimate, 70).

Positioning tilt (generic, historical): Historically, at this phase mix the phase-conditional optimum has favoured gold, Treasury duration and investment-grade credit, over mega-cap growth, developed international and emerging markets.

Phases are rules with the same thresholds in 2000 and today: Phase 2 = HY OAS +150bp or Baa-10y +50bp from the basket's peak; Phase 3 = Sahm rule or ISM < 47 for 3 months AND bank stress (KBW -25% or C&I charge-offs >= 1% and rising); Phase 4 = basket +20% off its low, above its 200-day average, HY 150bp off its wide. Odds come from every Nasdaq-100 drop since 1985 that reached today's depth, weighted by how closely its credit, macro and volatility readings matched today's, plus a small labelled judgment overlay for AI-credit stress. 'Ever P2+' = chance spreads cross the Phase-2 line at any point before the horizon. Model estimates on ~40 episodes: read them to within +/-10 points. Not financial advice.

⚔️Iran War

The conflict that began with joint US-Israeli strikes on Feb 28 is in a grinding, lower-intensity phase. The April two-week ceasefire is described as being on 'massive life support'. - **Strikes:** The US has carried out limited strikes on Qeshm Island. Trump calls them 'minor' and says they are not a return to full-scale war. - **Hormuz:** Shipping remains under attack. Iran says seven oil tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has severely restricted since the war began. The UAE rescued 22 crew in the Gulf of Oman as the US tightened its blockade of Iranian ports. - **Escalation signals:** The Revolutionary Guard says it has lifted its self-imposed 1,200-mile range limit on ballistic missiles. Israel's defense minister says 'the mission is still not complete'. - **Diplomacy:** Trump said on Nov 8 that fresh attacks would be 'highly unlikely' if Tehran strikes a nuclear deal and reopens Hormuz. Iran's latest proposal asks the US to end the naval blockade and sets aside the nuclear question. Iran's foreign minister warned of 'hell' if Washington chooses war. Trump says he expects to discuss the war with Xi and Putin at a China summit. Market read: today's -4.5% oil move is pricing the deal path. Continuing tanker attacks and the missile-range announcement mean the tail risk has not gone away. Reporting also links midterm results to the oil-below-$100 move.

🏦Fed Chair Warsh
NEAR TERM

Dec 8–9 FOMC: a 25bp hike from 3.75–4.00% is the base case. This is an analyst inference, not Warsh guidance. The Fed held on Oct 28 with Warsh calling inflation 'too high'. Two officials, Cook and Hammack, dissented for an immediate hike, and Warsh reportedly said raising sooner 'may be better'. Futures price about 77–85% odds of a hike after Friday's payrolls beat. Warsh has explicitly declined to give forward guidance, so a hold is a live minority risk if oil keeps falling.

~1 YEAR

Over about 12 months, the inference is a Fed that tightens 1–2 more times if Core PCE stays above 3%, then holds, while it shrinks its communication footprint. Warsh announced fewer rate-setting meetings: seven of eight from fall 2027 and six in 2028. That implies fewer but larger moves. A preference for a smaller balance sheet is an inference from his long-standing prior criticism of QE and was not re-verified in this session's searches. Earlier 2025–26 bank forecasts of Warsh cuts (Barclays, Morgan Stanley) predate the current inflation stance and look stale.

Warsh is running a less-guidance, data-reactive Fed with a hawkish lean. He holds back explicit signals, cuts back the meeting calendar, and lets the committee's hawks (Cook, Hammack) frame the debate. For markets this means front-end yields stay sticky (the 2Y did not rally today), the curve can steepen on oil relief, and policy surprises are more likely in size than in frequency. Any cut in the next year would likely require a growth shock: a Sahm trigger or HY breaking 448bp.
